Subjects must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO grade 4 glioma for which disease recurrence/progression after first line therapy is diagnosed by the treating physician.

candidate_evidence.quote: In this Phase I trial, it is proposed that sitagliptin will be used to inhibit Myeloid Derived Suppressor Cells (MDSCs) in recurrent Glioblastoma (GBM).

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Pilot: Change in participants' concentration of circulating MDSCs with treatment
provide preliminary evidence of sitagliptin in reducing infiltrating MDSCs in the GBM tumor microenvironment

role_evidence.quote: Sitagliptin, when combined with standard-of-care drug bevacizumab, is being tested to 1) find out if it is effective at treating gliomas that have returned or progressed after treatment

arms: Standard of care Bevacizumab in addition to Sitagliptin

role_evidence.quote: As this trial designed is for patients with recurrent GBM, patients will receive standard of care, bevacizumab, in addition to sitagliptin.

arms: Standard of care Bevacizumab in addition to Sitagliptin

biomarkers.biomarker_other: tumour single-cell sequencing, immune profiling and whole genome sequencing

source_quote.quote: Tumor tissue will undergo dissociation and single-cell sequencing, immune profiling, and whole genome sequencing.

arms: Standard of care Bevacizumab in addition to Sitagliptin

coder_notes: Eligibility requires WHO grade 4 glioma without an IDH requirement; per D27C this is historical glioblastoma (gbm_only, historical), and Glioblastoma is named in conditions. Note it could include IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma. Bevacizumab is standard-of-care background given to all patients (soc_backbone, single arm). Target engagement: circulating MDSC change (primary pilot outcome) and tumour-infiltrating MDSCs. MDSC measures are immune cell markers, not tumour molecular biomarkers, so not listed as biomarkers; only the tumour sequencing is listed as exploratory.
